title: Structured JSON sanitization on truncation with toolcall consistency
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Problem statement: When we stream structured JSON responses (text or function/tool call payloads), token-level truncation or mid-entity truncation frequently produces invalid JSON in the client stream. Existing recovery heuristics (close-open-brace stitching, naive quote escaping) cause two classes of failure: 1) downstream SDKs mis-interpret partial toolcall objects and either drop the call or attempt to execute a malformed call; 2) clients that expect strict JSON fail parsing and produce noisy errors rather than actionable retry tokens. This ticket designs and implements a sanitization + degradation protocol that preserves toolcall semantics where possible, exposes a compact resume token for client-driven retries, and provides a compatibility layer for older SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Runtime emits a structured 'partial-response' wrapper when truncation is detected mid-JSON instead of best-effort repair that changes semantics

2) If the truncated payload contains an in-progress function/tool call, the runtime signals CALL_TRUNCATED and includes a resume_token (opaque string) and fragment_digest so the client can request a continuation or replay without guessing the call arguments
3) New behavior is behind a compatibility flag (structured_truncation_v2) and defaults to on for hosted API; SDKs can opt-in to legacy_safe mode which receives a summary shim for older clients

4) Integration tests cover: stream truncation at string/array/object boundaries, truncation inside nested toolcall arguments, and simultaneous truncation across multiple toolcall boundaries with deterministic resume behavior
5) End-to-end latency overhead on p50 token generation is <2% for our benchmark workload, cost impact on throughput <3%
6) Backwards compatibility: clients that do not implement resume_token must receive a human-readable short summary and a stable error code (4223) so they can fallback gracefully
7) Runtime emits observability events for truncated-stream incidents with tags: model, route, customer_id, resume_available=true/false
decisions: Do not attempt to heuristically 'fix' JSON at the runtime layer when toolcall boundaries are ambiguous. Instead produce an explicit partial wrapper that preserves original bytes and provides resume metadata.
Introduce CALL_TRUNCATED sentinel to make tool-execution idempotent and explicit; tool runners must reject calls flagged with CALL_TRUNCATED unless a resume handshake completes.
Implement a compact resume_token (base64 of fragment id + offset + HMAC) signed by the control plane to avoid server-side state and still allow stateless resume requests.

Provide a legacy shim: when legacy_safe=true, runtime will also emit a short text-summary field 'legacy_summary' with highest-confidence top-level keys and truncated values (max 256 chars) to avoid breaking older SDKs.
Ship changes behind feature-flag structured_truncation_v2 for gradual rollout and metric comparison.
Security review: resume_token must be ephemeral (TTL 5 minutes) and not include customer PII in cleartext; HMAC secret rotated monthly.

comments: 2026-02-15 Ravi Patel: Initial triage meeting notes. Repro steps attached — truncation at 3 different offsets in toolcall.value caused two SDKs to either (a) execute malformed call or (b) crash JSON parser. Agreed we should avoid heuristic mutation when toolcall boundaries are present.

2026-02-18 Lena Morales: Spike completed. Implemented a prototype in branch spike/structured-truncation that wraps remainder bytes in a partial-response object. Verified client can re-request continuation with resume_token generated from ephemeral state in control plane. Perf impact negligible in synthetic test (~0.8% p50).

2026-02-22 Design review (Ben Chu): Reviewed wrapper format. Requested explicit CALL_TRUNCATED sentinel for toolcall semantics and a smaller resume token (32 bytes) to reduce payload overhead. Also asked for legacy_summary for older SDKs.

2026-02-28 Engineering sync: Decided HMAC-based resume_token rather than storing per-fragment state to minimize control plane storage. Lena to pick HMAC key rotation window and PRD updated with TTL 300s.
2026-03-03 PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234 — includes partial-response wrapper and resume token generator. Initial tests included.
2026-03-05 Perf run on canary cluster: p50 delta +0.9%, throughput delta -1.6%. These are within acceptance criteria. Included flamegraphs in the PR description.

2026-03-07 QA: Added fuzz harness; a run found a regression when truncation occurs inside escaped unicode sequence. Patch pushed to handle escape-aware truncation boundaries. Link to patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1241
